activities.title: Ways to Count at the Beach
activities.body: Counting at the beach can be done in different ways. Count each object one by one. You can also count shells, balloons, and bananas in bunches or groups. Children are encouraged to count in groups. Surbhi has collected seashells and wants to help make bracelets and necklaces. Her mother has made groups of shells for necklaces. Each shell necklace uses ten shells.
keyPoints: Objects can be counted one by one.
Objects can be counted in bunches or groups.
Each shell necklace uses ten shells.
activities.explanation: Groups make counting easier, and one-by-one counting also works.

activities.title: How Ten Strips Make 100
activities.body: Ten strips help us make 100. One example uses seven yellow strips and three red strips. It also has 70 yellow units and 30 red units. We can show the total with units or ten strips. Other combinations of ten strips can make a 100 units grid. A ten strip stands for ten units.

The example has 70 yellow units and 30 red units.
Units and ten strips can both show the total.
activities.explanation: Ten strips can show the total as 100 units.
